name: Vaporwave
editorial_article:
Vaporwave is an internet-born microgenre, aesthetic, and cultural phenomenon that crystallized in the early 2010s, emerging as a surrealist and often ironic commentary on consumer capitalism, digital nostalgia, and the detritus of late-20th-century pop culture. Musically, it is defined by the heavy manipulation of source material—typically smooth jazz, elevator music, 80s/90s R&B, and lounge tracks—which are slowed down, chopped, and rearranged to evoke a ghostly, hypnagogic atmosphere. This aesthetic of "hauntology" transforms the optimistic, corporate-sponsored sounds of the past into something uncanny and dreamlike, reflecting a collective obsession with the failed promises of technological utopia.

The movement is intrinsically linked to its visual language, which thrives on a curated mix of Web 1.0 design, Memphis-style geometric patterns, anime clips, and stark, rendered 3D environments featuring classical statuary. By repurposing the advertising motifs and corporate jingles of the 1980s and 90s, vaporwave artists create a sonic landscape that feels both comfortingly familiar and deeply alien. While initially centered on ironic detachment and critical reflection, the genre rapidly expanded into a sprawling ecosystem of subgenres—including Mallsoft, Future Funk, and Signalwave—each iterating on the core premise of memory, obsolescence, and the digital afterlife. Its influence extends far beyond music, shaping internet meme culture and defining a specific visual dialect of post-internet art that continues to resonate today.
editorial_definition: An internet-native music genre and aesthetic that emerged in the early 2010s, characterized by the manipulation of 1980s and 1990s pop, lounge, and corporate music into surreal, nostalgic, and often ironic soundscapes.
